survivors.name: no-goals-equality
survivors.binding: Proposer's directions are correct; tighten wording. Load-bearing arbitrage relation (EXACT, rule-guaranteed, tradeable): P(SCORE-0-0) = 1 - P(TOTAL-Over0.5), equivalently SCORE-0-0 YES ≡ TOTAL-Over0.5 NO. FTTS leg is NOT an equality "up to a caveat" — it is a strict one-directional SUBSET: FTTS-NONE YES ⟹ SCORE-0-0 YES (and ⟹ TOTAL-Over0.5 NO), never the converse, so P(FTTS-NONE) ≤ P(SCORE-0-0) = 1 - P(TOTAL-Over0.5). Trade FTTS-NONE only as the cheap side of that inequality (short FTTS-NONE vs long TOTAL-Over0.5 has bounded downside; the reverse is unbounded when a 0-0 regulation game scores in ET). In Leagues Cup 2026 the inequality is empirically tight (no ET) but that is not a rule guarantee.
survivors.detection: Join by game-key. SCORE leg where custom_strike home_score=0 & away_score=0, the TOTAL leg 'Over 0.5' (suffix -1), and FTTS 'No Goal' leg (suffix -NONE). Assert P(SCORE-0-0)=1-P(TOTAL-Over0.5); flag FTTS-NONE as one-directional superset check.

SCORE 0-0 cell (KXLEAGUESCUPSCORE-...-PHI0NCX0): "If the result is a 0-0 draw ... after 90 minutes plus stoppage time (does not include extra time or penalties), then the market resolves to Yes." TOTAL Over 0.5 (KXLEAGUESCUPTOTAL-...-1): "If over 0.5 goals are scored ... after 90 minutes plus stoppage time (does not include extra time or penalties), then the market resolves to Yes." Both legs cite the SAME regulation-only window verbatim; goals are non-negative integers so "over 0.5" ≡ "≥1 goal" ≡ "not 0-0". They partition the outcome space exactly => P(SCORE-0-0)+P(TOTAL-Over0.5)=1, i.e. SCORE-0-0 YES = TOTAL-Over0.5 NO. Machine check: 31/31 games have SCORE-0-0 and TOTAL-1 both regulation-only, and TOTAL-1 is exactly "Over 0.5" in 31/31. survivors.name: tennis-exactscore-refines-match
survivors.binding: REFINEMENT / one-directional nesting, not a full partition-equality. Correct part: each KX*EXACTMATCH leg <PLAYER><setscore> implies the corresponding KX*MATCH-<PLAYER> leg (subset), giving the arbitrage-safe bound P(exact leg) <= P(match-winner leg), robust because both markets share the same 'after a ball has been played' void trigger. INCORRECT part (drop it): 'winner's exact-score legs sum to P(MATCH winner) exactly.' A mid-match retirement/walkover/default awards the match to the opponent (MATCH resolves cleanly) but produces a non-2-set finishing score absent from the {2-0,2-1} menu, so all exact legs resolve No and the sum falls short of the moneyline. The menu is exhaustive over NATURALLY COMPLETED best-of-3 finishes, not over MATCH-WINNING finishes; retirement wins have no exact-score leg. The proposer's flagged failure mode (best-of-5 menu incompleteness) is real but secondary — the equality fails even with a 'complete' best-of-3 menu.

For each KXATPEXACTMATCH/KXWTAEXACTMATCH leg <PLAYER><setscore> emit implication to KX*MATCH-<PLAYER>; sum same-winner legs to compare against the moneyline.

survivors.name: mlb-player-stat-dominance
survivors.binding: No direction correction needed — all 7 edges and both exclusions are correct as claimed, exactness is deterministic at the stat level. Add two operational qualifiers: (a) the price inequality is a hard arbitrage bound only conditional on the shared live-settlement branch; under the identical 'fair market price' void clause both legs void together, leaving bounded basis risk rather than a clean unbounded arb, so treat it as a strong dominance/quasi-arb, not a pure static arb. (b) Only emit an edge when BOTH legs exist at the same k — in particular any HIT->TB or HR->TB edge exists only for k>=2 (no TB-1 market), so the 'P(Hits k+)<=P(TB k+)' example is vacuous at k=1.
survivors.detection: Player node key = (game-key, player-id) parsed from ticker suffix, shared verbatim across KXMLBHR/KXMLBHIT/KXMLBTB/KXMLBRBI/KXMLBHRR (e.g. AZCCARROLL7). For the same (player,game,k) emit edges per the fixed DAG: HR->{HIT,RBI,TB,HRR}, HIT->{TB,HRR}, RBI->HRR.
survivors.evidence: All five example legs settle on the same subject/game with "records k+" semantics, verbatim from the data. HIT: "If Corbin Carroll records 1+ hits in the San Diego vs Arizona ... game ... resolves to Yes." TB: "records 2+ total bases". HR: "records 1+ home runs". RBI: "records 1+ RBIs". HRR: "records 1+ total hits + runs + rbis" (so HRR = H+R+RBI). Each of the 7 DAG edges is a HARD pointwise MLB inequality at a common k, giving {A>=k} ⊆ {B>=k} ⟹ P(A k+) <= P(B k+): HR<=HITS (a HR is by rule a hit), HR<=RBI (a HR always credits the batter >=1 RBI), HR<=TB (1 HR = 4 bases), HR<=HRR (HR<=H<=HRR), HITS<=TB (each hit >=1 base), HITS<=HRR (R,RBI>=0), RBI<=HRR (H,R>=0). No MLB scoring state reverses any edge (a legit HR that yields 0 RBI or isn't a hit does not exist; if a batter is called out passing a runner it is no longer scored a HR). The two deliberately-excluded edges are correctly excluded: TB->HRR fails (a solo double = TB 2 but HRR 1) and HITS<->RBI is genuinely independent (single with 0 RBI vs sac-fly RBI with 0 hits). Join key is sound: custom_strike.baseball_player UUID 73c3c2e2-ad65-411d-8b66-a95578c6d4aa is byte-identical across all five series and the suffix AZCCARROLL7 maps to exactly one UUID; each of the 5 SDAZ players appears in all 5 series; rules name the subject explicitly (no boilerplate-omits-subject trap).

Two refinements, not corrections: (1) The alignment must be done on RESOLVED rule thresholds, i.e. match each range bucket's inclusive UPPER edge (the "between LO-HI" HI, e.g. 51999.99 / 0.5399) to a ladder "above HI" threshold — NOT on yes_sub_title/lower-bound display labels, which drift (XRP ladder shows 0.51991 for the >=0.52 rung). For running-max/touch legs (BTC case) it is exact ONLY conditional on higher-strike-window being a SUBSET of lower-strike-window; the scanner must verify byte-level window bounds, not merely 'same year/same end date'. Group key must be (underlying, EXACT window bounds [start,end] for touch OR exact instant for point-in-time, byte-identical source clause) with observation mode kept as part of the source-clause byte match — never normalize touch and point-in-time to the same resolution timestamp. Distinct from L-threshold: this crosses event/series boundaries (KXSOL26500 != KXSOLD26; KXBTC2026250 != KXBTC2026200), where order books are not auto-coupled — a real, non-duplicate family.

Within a group, any two markets with strike_type='greater' and floors f1>f2 nest (f1 implies f2); with strike_type='less' the direction reverses. Distinct from L-threshold which is confined to legs inside one event.

rejected.name: count-subset-tail-dominance

Take the degenerate distribution where this is certain: P(cuts>=2)=1 but P(changes>=2)=0, so the claimed P(changes>=k) >= P(cuts>=k) becomes 0>=1, FALSE — changes does NOT stochastically dominate cuts. State B (opposite): one 25bp hike, no cuts -> changes=1, cuts=0, so changes>cuts. Only the lower link survives: every 25bp emergency-meeting cut increment is also a 2026 cut increment, so cuts_total(w) >= emergency(w) in every settlement state -> P(cuts>=k) >= P(emergency>=k) is genuinely rule-forced and tradeable (YES on emergency-tail implies YES on cuts-tail; sum of emergency legs T_k.. <= sum of cuts legs T_k..). Secondary defect: FEDCHGCOUNT says only 'before 2027' with no explicit Jan-1-2026 start bound, a possible window mismatch, but the unit mismatch alone is fatal so this is not load-bearing.

After certification but before the nomination is formalized, A dies/withdraws/is DQ'd; the Florida Republican Executive Committee names C (the runner-up) as the replacement nominee -> nominee leg for C resolves YES. Now P(C 2nd)+P(C nominee)=2>1. Feasible in the real data because the nominee market stays open to 2026-11-03, months after the primary certification that already settled the place leg. The nominee leg's empty rules_secondary and its "wins the nomination" trigger (not "finishes 1st") admit this path. Ties/proportional resolution do not save exactness either; the anti-nominee link is a plurality convention, not a settlement identity.

rejected.name: seatcount-vs-district-winners
rejected.why: Two independent breaks. (1) DIRECTION: the claimed "E0(Yes) => every district -R resolves Yes" is false. E0 only says 0 Democrats; the other seats need not all be Republican. Concrete state: TN elects 8 Republicans and one district's winner dies before seating, leaving that seat vacant at term start. WINSTATE counts 0 Democrats (rules_secondary: vacant/unfilled seats are not counted as won), so E0 = Yes; but that district's -R leg resolves No (no Republican is "sworn in"), and -D also No. The R-implication breaks. Same break with a third-party/independent winner (the series structurally lists such candidates), where -R = No while Dems stay at 0. (2) MEAN IDENTITY is unrealizable on every listed instance: replicating the realized seat count S requires holding k units of each singleton bucket E_k, but the top bucket is "Above 2" (flat $1 for S in {3..9}), so S>=3 cannot be replicated; FL additionally has an open "Below 4" bucket. Every one of the 6 live menus is open-ended, so the "sum of D-race prices = sum_k k*P(k)" arbitrage binds ZERO real instances. Coverage also fails outright for UT (1/4) and FL (26/28), so the district portfolio cannot even be assembled there.

rejected.name: intraday-implies-dailyhigh
rejected.why: Two concrete settlement states break it with ZERO rule violation. (1) HARD, Chicago Aug 3 2026: The Weather Company reports KORD (O'Hare) 4 PM = 84.0°F, so KXTEMPCHIH-26AUG0316-T83.99 (">83.99", i.e. >=84) resolves YES; the NWS Climatological Report for Chicago MIDWAY (KMDW) posts a daily max of 83°F, so the daily "max>=84" composite (KXHIGHCHI-...-T83 bin) resolves NO. Different stations ~15 mi apart, no rule links them — intraday-YES coexists with daily-below-threshold. (2) SOFT, NYC same station: TWC reports KNYC 4 PM = 80°F, so KXTEMPNYCH-26AUG0316-T79.99 resolves YES; the NWS official Central Park Climatological daily max is 79°F after its own QC/rounding, so the daily "max>=80" composite resolves NO. The intraday rules_secondary itself concedes TWC values carry "rounding and conversion differences from the final reported value," so a 1°F TWC-vs-NWS disagreement straddling the traded cut point is anticipated and rule-permitted, not an anomaly. Because the "max dominates any single reading" inequality is a property of ONE measurement series and these legs are always settled by two independent authorities, no joint-settlement lock exists — the family is breakable on every city, hardest on Chicago.
